items.t: Vedder Crossing takes its name from a bridge: the Province of BC uses Vedder Crossing Bridge, where Vedder Road crosses the river, as the dividing point between the Chilliwack River upstream of the bridge and the Vedder River between the bridge and the Vedder Canal.

The City does not publish an MLS-style boundary for Vedder Crossing: the closest official description is the South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan area, bordered by the Chilliwack/Vedder River to the south, the Promontory neighbourhood to the southeast, Tzeachten First Nations Lands to the east, Vedder Road to the west and the broader Vedder Neighbourhood to the north.

The South Vedder Neighbourhood Plan was adopted by Council in 2022 and updated in 2025 as part of the Official Community Plan update, and the City describes South Vedder as part of the broader Vedder Neighbourhood at the south end of Chilliwack.

Vedder Park, on the river at 45450 Petawawa Road, sits on the paved Legacy Trail, connects to the Garrison Crossing community to the north, and is within walking distance of the University of the Fraser Valley (UFV) Chilliwack campus.

blocks.text: Vedder Crossing: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The river sets the building rule here: the City states there are floodplain areas in the city for both the Fraser River and the Vedder River, and the provincial dike standard and floodplain mapping for the Vedder River are based on the 1-in-200-year flood event.
New building near the river is governed by Floodplain Regulation Bylaw No. 4519, which sets flood construction levels for the Vedder River and Vedder Canal floodplains.

blocks.text: Vedder Crossing: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The river fills with sediment and the City removes it as flood work: the City states sediment removal from the Vedder River restores the river's capacity to contain and convey floodwater, and that the November 2021 event deposited 10 times the typical annual amount of sediment.

The Province puts a number on that event: the November 2021 atmospheric river deposited 440,000 cubic metres of sediment in the Vedder River between Vedder Crossing and the Highway 1 bridge, reducing flood conveyance capacity.
Vedder flood timing is the opposite of the Fraser River's: the Province states Vedder River and Canal flood flows are typically governed by fall and winter storm events rather than freshet.
There is a named river gauge for this crossing: a Water Survey of Canada gauge named "Chilliwack River Near Vedder Crossing" is listed on the City's Vedder River Flood Protection page.
Qoqó:lem Park at 45076 Vedder Mountain Road is the second river-side park on this side, named in a City press release alongside the Vedder Park works.
The Vedder Park site itself is leftover base land: the City states the site was previously used as a military base, and Garrison Crossing is the community to its north.

The Cheam Leisure Centre at 45501 Market Way is the recreation centre for this side of the city, in Sardis north of Vedder Crossing, and there is no Fraser Valley Regional Library branch in Vedder Crossing itself — the Sardis Library at 5819 Tyson Road is the south-side branch.
Route 56 Cultus Lake is a summer-only service (July 1 to Labour Day) and stops on Vedder Road at Watson Road, so it is not a year-round option for a car-free household here.

blocks.text: Vedder Crossing: development and new projects

items.t: Vedder River flood protection works — City of Chilliwack / Vedder River Management Area Committee: raising the West Dike (right bank) by approximately one metre, designed for the Vedder River 1:200-year flood event with 0.75 metres of freeboard, plus planned sediment removals by the Vedder River Management Area Committee to maintain floodway capacity.
44490 Keith Wilson Road apartment rezoning (application RZ001796, Zoning Bylaw Amendment Bylaw 2026, No. 5530) sits in this neighbourhood.
Status: plan in effect (as of November 3, 2026).
City utility and solid waste charges here are billed quarterly, under the same City bylaws as the rest of Chilliwack.

Route 51 Vedder is the local bus and the system's Frequent Transit Network route: it runs between the UFV Chilliwack Campus and Downtown Chilliwack via Vedder Road, through the middle of this neighbourhood.
BC Transit added later weekday and weekend service and more frequent Saturday-evening service on Route 51 from January 4, 2026.
The system's other south-side routes also run from this corridor: Route 54 Promontory, Route 55 Yarrow-Greendale and Route 58 Tyson all serve the Sardis and Vedder side of the city.
BC Transit's Chilliwack Rider's Guide map labels the "VEDDER CROSSING" stop area at the south end of Vedder Road, at the river crossing itself.

The distinction matters when a buyer reads flood documents, because City and provincial pages use both names for the same river system on either side of the bridge.
faq.q: Why does the river change its name at the bridge?

The City posts trail closure notices for flood-recovery work on its Vedder Trail page, so trail access at a given address can be interrupted by river work even in a normal year.
